newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST - Good half seen for FCL Building.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Good half seen for FCL Building.

text.p: Robust first half earnings in the region of NZ$65-75 million are expected for Fletcher Building when it reports its first half result next week, analysts said on Friday.

While that would represent a decline from NZ$77 million in the half year to December 1995, analysts said comparability was limited due, among other things, to discontinuaton or sale of various businesses.
FCL Building has operations in concrete, steel, plasterboard, medium density fibreboard (MDF), aluminium extrusion, distribution and construction.
Most of these are expected to report solid earnings, apart from the MDF operation in Rotorua. There were also doubts about distribution (Placemakers), where there was intense competition.
But the market has welcomed the company's decisions to exit many of its loss-making international operations to focus on New Zealand.

FCL Building's decision to buy the Comalco-Carter Holt Harvey aluminium extrusion business and the pipe and drainage business of Humes Industries from Adelaide Brighton Cement were both also seen as auguring well for the future.
Along with FCL Energy, analysts regard FCL Building highly, while the other "letter" stocks, FCL Forests and Paper, suffer the vagaries of the commodities cycle.
David Stanley at Doyle Paterson Brown said FCL Building had a series of strong businesses in one geographic area, New Zealand, where there was a high barrier to entry.
"They have very strong market positions. Management have also performed extremely well in continuing to refocus and re-shape those business groupings," Stanley said.
Analysts said clear evidence was emerging that New Zealand would be increasing its spending on infrastructure, due in part to undertakings by the new centre-right coalition government.

There were some big projects in store for the future, namely the proposed Britomart development in Auckland and the NZ$200 million Manapouri hydro scheme upgrade. FCL Building will lead the consortium that won the contract.
John Cairns at Cavill White Securities said FCL Building had the luxury of operating either as a monopolist or in a duopoly in many of its key areas, where margins were also strong.
With the prospect of high infrastructural spending, there was also the likelihood of deferred spending bearing fruit.
"All the divisions will do pretty well, at least on par with last year, on an adjusted basis, except for panels and distribution," Mary Watson at First NZ Capital said.

"Overall it will be a good result. Remember also that the economy has slowed very sharply from June to December," she said. Watson agreed that prospects for central and local government spending on infrastructure looked promising.
"Spends in capital intensive industries like forestry, dairying and energy, look very strong. In most cases it's a question of modernisation -- do it or you lose it," she said.
